title: Pass 3 reference table — Lockhart-growing hexagonal leaf blade mesh and sequential vein-order emergence for Slot 035 (feugier-carrier-driven-canalization)
organism: Arabidopsis thaliana (first-leaf lamina, procambial venation orders 1-4)

bibliographic_corrections.verified_value: Journal of Theoretical Biology 236(4):366-375 (2005), published 21 October 2005
bibliographic_corrections.verified_against: Crossref works API and PubMed efetch, 2026-10-20

primary_sources.citation: Feugier FG, Mochizuki A, Iwasa Y (2005) Self-organization of the vascular system in plant leaves: inter-dependent dynamics of auxin flux and carrier proteins. J. Theor. Biol. 236(4):366-375
reported_results_used: Result 1: branching auxin distribution patterns self-organize on a hexagonal lattice with uniform auxin production and a single marginal petiole sink cell.
Result 2: response functions that accelerate (carrier number increases faster than flux) generate branching patterns; linear or decelerating response functions form NO branching pattern.
Result 3: when membrane domains compete for a limited cellular pool of carriers, auxin is more abundant in veins than in surrounding tissue.

primary_sources.citation: Scarpella E, Francis P, Berleth T (2004) Stage-specific markers define early steps of procambium development in Arabidopsis leaves and correlate termination of vein formation with mesophyll differentiation. Development 131(14):3445-3455
reported_results_used: Preprocambial domains are always continuous with pre-existing vasculature; veins are initiated as freely ending preprocambial domains and the network forms by subsequent fusion of these domains.

Vein orders arise reiteratively (new preprocambial branches) during blade expansion until mesophyll differentiation terminates the process; interrupting extension yields fewer vein orders and more freely ending veins.

primary_sources.citation: Scarpella E, Marcos D, Friml J, Berleth T (2006) Control of leaf vascular patterning by polar auxin transport. Genes Dev. 20(8):1015-1027
reported_results_used: Epidermal PIN1 convergence points at the margin initiate secondary veins; transient bipolar PIN1 cells bridge nascent strands to pre-existing veins.

primary_sources.citation: Kang J, Dengler N (2004) Vein pattern development in adult leaves of Arabidopsis thaliana. Int. J. Plant Sci. 165(2):231-242
reported_results_used: Vein orders (midvein, secondary, tertiary, quaternary / higher order) are initiated sequentially during lamina expansion.

primary_sources.citation: Lockhart JA (1965) An analysis of irreversible plant cell elongation. J. Theor. Biol. 8(2):264-275
reported_results_used: Irreversible (plastic) cell expansion rate (1/V) dV/dt = phi (P - Y) for turgor P above the wall yield threshold Y; zero below.

primary_sources.citation: Kuchen EE, Fox S, Barbier de Reuille P, Kennaway R, Bensmihen S, Avondo J, Calder GM, Southam P, Robinson S, Bangham A, Coen E (2012) Generation of leaf shape through early patterns of growth and tissue polarity. Science 335(6072):1092-1096
reported_results_used: Early Arabidopsis leaf primordia are narrow and widen allometrically as the lamina expands (used to motivate the g^1.5 width / g^0.5 length mask allometry; exponents are a reduced modelling choice, not fitted to this paper).

lockhart_growth_law.equation: (1/A) dA/dt = phi * max(0, P_turgor - Y(t)),  Y(t) = Y0 + kappa * t
lockhart_growth_law.closed_form: A(t)/A0 = exp(phi * ((P - Y0) t - kappa t^2 / 2)) for t <= (P - Y0)/kappa, constant afterwards
lockhart_growth_law.note: Parameter values are illustrative (order-of-magnitude for growing tissues: P 0.3-0.8 MPa, Y 0.1-0.3 MPa); the stage schedule follows the qualitative chronology of Scarpella et al. (2004) first leaves. The blade mesh grows by marginal cell addition; no cell-expansion or viscoelastic wall mechanics are modelled.

accelerating_open_tree.source: Feugier et al. (2005) results 1-2 (accelerating Phi = J^2, conserved pool)

accelerating_committed_reticulate.source: Feugier (2005) Phi = J^2 + Scarpella et al. (2004) irreversible procambial commitment of fusing preprocambial domains
accelerating_committed_reticulate.note: Reference loop count is not taken from an external specimen; the test is beta_1 >= 1 with beta_1 monotonically decreasing in tau_commit (Spearman rho -> -1).

decelerating_no_branching.source: Feugier et al. (2005) result 2: linear or decelerating response -> no branching pattern
decelerating_no_branching.note: A diffuse, (near-)uniformly polarized sheet; measured as the fraction of blade cells whose maximal membrane face exceeds P_vein.

sequential_emergence_reference.source: Scarpella, Francis & Berleth (2004) Development 131:3445-3455; Kang & Dengler (2004) Int. J. Plant Sci. 165:231-242
sequential_emergence_reference.statement: Midvein, secondary, tertiary and quaternary veins appear in that order during blade expansion; higher orders are initiated only while the blade is still expanding.
